# Walkito

> A 12-week exercise program for heel and foot pain. The plan adapts
> daily to logged pain and walking load, and measures progress with physical
> retests every two weeks rather than by asking how you feel.

## Core pages
- [Exercises for plantar fasciitis](https://walkito.site/plantar-fasciitis-exercises/):
  heel raises and stretches with doses, what the 2023 guideline grades A and B,
  and what it advises against
- [Exercises for flat feet](https://walkito.site/flat-feet-exercises/): short-foot,
  toe, balance and hip work for flexible flat feet, and how long the arch takes
- [The 12-week program](https://walkito.site/program/): block structure,
  session frequency, how the plan adapts, what the retests measure
- [Evidence](https://walkito.site/science/): the trials and the 2023 clinical
  guideline the program follows, with stated limitations
- [Questions](https://walkito.site/faq/): session length, missed days, Apple
  Health permissions, notifications, the streak
- [Support](https://walkito.site/support/): notifications, Apple Health
  permissions, subscriptions, deleting your data
- [Privacy](https://walkito.site/privacy/): what stays on the device and what
  leaves it
- [Terms of use](https://walkito.site/terms/): the licence, App Store billing
  and cancellation, health and safety, and what the app does not promise

## Key facts
- Programme length: 12 weeks, six blocks of 14 days
- Session length: 3 to 8 minutes; three strength days a week, one prescribed
  rest day in seven
- Retests every 14 days measure calf endurance, arch hold and single-leg
  balance — 3 tests, 4 minutes
- The plan steps back a level on a high-pain morning and returns when pain
  settles; it never accelerates on a good day
- A day counts as attended if pain was logged, a session was finished, or the
  plan prescribed rest
- iOS only. It reads Apple Health for steps, walking speed, walking asymmetry,
  flights climbed, heart rate, resting heart rate, active energy, sleep and
  workouts, all optional, and never uploads it
- Health data is summarised on the device and is never uploaded

## Notes
Walkito provides exercise programming. It does not diagnose or treat any
condition. Sharp or worsening pain should be seen by a clinician.

## Full text
The complete text of the program and questions pages is at
https://walkito.site/llms-full.txt

## Key findings the program follows
- High-load strength training scored 29 points lower on the Foot Function Index
  than stretching at 3 months (95% CI 6-52, p=0.016); at 12 months the two had
  converged, so the effect is speed rather than a larger result
- A 6-week program improved navicular drop by 0.4 cm and arch angle by 16
  degrees in people with *flexible* flat feet
- Only short-foot programs longer than 6 weeks improved navicular drop
- The 2023 JOSPT guideline grades stretching A, strength B, orthotics-alone B
  (not in isolation), and therapeutic ultrasound A - do not use
- Gait asymmetry did not predict injury in a trial of 800+ runners

## Not yet published
There is no aggregate-user-outcome data on this site. It does not exist rather
than being withheld.
